steps.title: Configure TIRF microscope and lasers
steps.instruction: Place the TIRF microscope on an air‑gapped table, verify laser alignment and TIRF illumination before each session, and ensure the system has a 100‑x objective (NA ≥ 1.4) and a scientific CMOS camera meeting or exceeding the specifications of a Photometrics Prime BSI (4.2 MP, 6.5 µm pixels, 18.8 mm FOV, 12‑bit, QE ≈ 95 %, dark current 0.5 e⁻/pixel·s, read noise 1.0 e⁻, ≥30 fps). Use laser lines 488 nm/561 nm/640 nm at nominal powers 70 mW/60 mW/50 mW (adjust exposure times for single‑frame settings).

steps.title: Prepare imaging chamber and perfusion system
steps.instruction: Mount a 25 mm glass coverslip in a quick‑release magnetic or non‑magnetic imaging chamber (Warner Instruments #QR‑40LP; aperture 19.7 mm, buffer volume ≈ 310 µL) or an equivalent chamber (Warner #RC‑21BRW or Ibidi μ‑dish Grid‑500 #81168). Place the chamber in a Warner microincubator (#DH‑40iL) on the objective, connect its perfusion ports to a syringe pump (Fusion 100‑X Touch, KR Analytical or equivalent) for controlled buffer flow (optional: add/remove reagents with a pipette). Acquire test images of fluorescent calibration beads to confirm optimal TIRF alignment.

steps.title: Dissect and homogenize rat forebrain tissue
steps.instruction: Timing ≈ 25–30 min. Euthanize an adult rat (6–8 months) according to institutional guidelines, dissect the forebrain into ice‑cold PBS containing phosphatase and protease inhibitor cocktail, and keep all tools on ice. Homogenize the tissue in 2 mL ice‑cold homogenization buffer (0.32 M sucrose, 4 mM HEPES, pH 7.4, plus inhibitors) using a 2 mL glass‑Teflon homogenizer for 15–17 gentle strokes. Rinse the homogenizer with an additional 2 mL buffer and combine for a total volume of 4 mL.

steps.title: Enrich synaptosomes by differential centrifugation
steps.instruction: Timing ≈ 3 h. Centrifuge the 4 mL homogenate at 1,500 × g for 10 min at 4 °C (pellet P1). Transfer the supernatant (S1) to a clean tube and centrifuge at 16,100 × g for 20 min at 4 °C (pellet P2). Resuspend P2 in 1 mL homogenization buffer. Prepare a two‑step discontinuous sucrose gradient in an ultracentrifuge tube: 4.5 mL of 1.2 M sucrose (4 mM HEPES + inhibitors) overlaid with 4 mL of 0.8 M sucrose (4 mM HEPES + inhibitors); layer the resuspended P2 on top of the 0.8 M layer. Ultracentrifuge at 20,000 rpm (≈68,800 × g) for 70 min at 4 °C using a swing‑bucket rotor (Beckman Optima‑90, acceleration/deceleration ramp 3). Collect the synaptosome‑enriched (SYN) fraction at the 0.8 M/1.2 M interface (≈0.7–1 mL). Aliquot 50–100 µL portions for later homogenate preparation and keep the remainder on ice for vesicle isolation (or store 1:1 in Syn‑PER at 4 °C overnight).

steps.title: Isolate synaptic vesicle pellet from synaptosomes
steps.instruction: Timing ≈ 1 h. Mechanically disrupt the SYN fraction with a #23 needle attached to a 1 mL syringe (21 strokes). Sonicate on ice with 1–2 pulses of 2 s each, 30 s intervals. Centrifuge the mixture at 21,000 g for 10 min at 4 °C to remove large debris, then transfer the supernatant and centrifuge again at 21,000 g for 20 min at 4 °C to pellet the synaptic vesicle pellet (SV‑P).

steps.title: Purify synaptic vesicles via sucrose gradient
steps.instruction: Timing ≈ 3.5–4 h. Resuspend the SV‑P in 0.5–1 mL 0.32 M sucrose + 4 mM HEPES (pH 7.4). Prepare a discontinuous gradient in an ultracentrifuge tube: bottom 3 mL 1.2 M sucrose, middle 5 mL 0.8 M sucrose, top 1 mL 0.32 M sucrose containing the resuspended pellet. Centrifuge at 100,000 × g for 70 min at 4 °C (acceleration/deceleration 3). Collect the vesicle‑enriched band at the 0.8 M/1.2 M interface (≈0.3–0.5 mL). Dilute this fraction 1:3 with Syn‑PER buffer, then centrifuge at 37,000 × g for 45 min at 4 °C. Resuspend the final pellet in 100–200 µL storage buffer (Syn‑PER with 0.1 % DMSO and 0.1 % glycerol). Aliquot ~25 µL and store at –20 °C; thaw aliquots on ice for immediate use.

steps.title: Prepare synaptosome homogenate lysate
steps.instruction: Timing ≈ 1.5 h. Thaw a frozen SYN aliquot (step 4g) on ice and resuspend in a 1:2 dilution of ice‑cold lysis buffer (50 mM Tris‑HCl pH 7.4, 500 mM NaCl, 1 % NP‑40, 0.5 % sodium deoxycholate, 0.1 % SDS, 2 mM EDTA, 1 mM DTT, plus phosphatase and protease inhibitors). Optional: add CHAPS 0.5–1 % or digitonin 0.1–0.5 %; increase NaCl up to 500 mM or SDS to 0.5 % for harsher extraction. Sonicate on ice (3 × 10 s pulses, 30 s intervals). Centrifuge at 21,000 × g for 20–30 min at 4 °C, collect the supernatant (soluble proteins), and determine protein concentration using a BCA assay (Thermo Fisher #23227). Aliquot 50–100 µg protein per tube and store at –20 °C (stable ≥1 year).

steps.title: Optional: Perform ELISA validation assays
steps.instruction: Follow the chosen ELISA format (indirect, sandwich, or customized sandwich) using the following common steps: (a) Coat/ capture primary antibody (75 µL, 0.05–0.1 mg well⁻¹) and incubate 2 h at RT or 16 h at 4 °C; (b) Block with 100 µL 1 mg mL⁻¹ BSA for 2 h at RT; (c) Add antigen (50–60 µL of SYN or SV homogenate, 0.05–0.1 mg well⁻¹) and incubate 2 h at RT or 16 h at 4 °C; (d) Wash: invert plate, tap dry, add 100 µL 1× PBS, discard; repeat 2 quick washes and 2 washes with 5 min incubations; (e) Add secondary antibody (50–60 µL streptavidin‑HRP, 1:1,000–1:5,000) and incubate 2 h at RT; (f) Add 30 µL TMB substrate, develop 2–15 min at RT until blue; (g) Stop with 30 µL 4 M H₂SO₄ (yellow); (h) Shake 5 s, read absorbance at 450 nm (background 620 nm) on a Tecan Spark M10. Run technical duplicates/triplicates; repeat if variation > 5 %. For low‑signal samples, use Revvity ELAST amplification (#NEP116001EA) per manufacturer’s instructions.

steps.title: Process TIRF images and quantify vesicle density
steps.instruction: Use Fiji‑ImageJ (or equivalent) to subtract background fluorescence using blank coverslip images (camera offset, autofluorescence, buffer fluorescence). Average background from 6–10 images per batch and apply subtraction via a batch macro (e.g., Analyze Particles). Include only fields of view with uniform illumination and no artefacts. Count fluorescent puncta per FOV or per µm² across at least 10–15 FOVs per condition per replicate (minimum three independent surface functionalizations). Stop acquisition if background varies > 10 % between identical coverslips or if vesicle aggregation/lysis is observed. Report vesicle density as mean ± SD or SEM and perform appropriate statistical tests.

description: This protocol describes the single-molecule pull-down (SIM-Pull) assay and imaging of synaptic protein complexes and vesicle recruitment using a total internal reflection fluorescence (TIRF) microscope. The instructions below outline the essential setup for the microscope, imaging hardware, and sample chambers required to reproduce the experiments described in this study. Although demonstrated here for 25 mm coverslips mounted in a manual mount imaging chamber, the protocol can also be adapted with appropriate modifications depending on user preference.1.TIRF microscope and imaging platform.a.Ensure that the microscope and laser lines are installed on an air-gapped table to limit vibration that will impact image acquisition.b.Always check laser alignment and confirm TIRF illumination before each imaging session to ensure consistent single-molecule excitation.c.Ensure that your microscope is equipped with a 100-x objective (N/A 1.4 or higher) and scientific CMOS (sCMOS) camera (or equivalent) offering high sensitivity, low noise, and fast acquisition suitable for single-molecule TIRF image acquisition.Note: The data in this study was acquired using a Photometrics Prime BSI with the following specifications, 4.2-megapixel, 6.5 x 6.5 μm pixel size, and maximum field of view (FOV) 18.8 mm, 12-bit dynamic range, quantum efficiency ∼95%, 0.5 e−/p/s dark current, 1.0 e− read noise and readout speed of ≥30 frames s-1 (please see: https://www.teledynevisionsolutions.com/products/prime-bsi/?vertical=tvs-photometrics&segment=tvs). An equivalent camera should meet or exceed these specifications for reliable single-fluorophore detection. Additionally, the laser intensities out of the box are 488/561/640 nm = 70/60/50 mW, which will have some percentage of loss when passing through the fiber. Laser exposure times were adjusted according to the recommended single-frame settings.2.Set up the imaging chamber and perfusion system.Note: For this protocol we used 25 mm glass coverslips
